pr_title: testsuite: coverage: Fix gcov broken output on qemu_x86
pr_body:
Fix an issue introduced with #63826 by bc8b7dd6dd at qemu_x86
when gcov data was broken because of optimized out memcpy() in write_u64() static inline function.

Fixes #64396 
Alternative fix: #64406
pr_comments: #64406 is a workaround for the same issue to ignore gcov's corrupted data at gcovr (newer version with additional command line option).

Interesting.
I am unable to reproduce this error. Just used the command from the bug description and generated coverage for this function:

> @nordic-piks, it looks like GCC optimized out `if { memcpy() }` branch and only `print_u32()` are left at `write_u64()`. My first quick fix was wrapping this function into '-O0' like this:
> 
> ```
> #pragma GCC push_options
> #pragma GCC optimize("O0")
> static inline void write_u64( ... ) {
> ...
> }
> #pragma GCC pop_options
> ```

I just upgraded gcovr to 6.0 (leaving all other versions the same) and got the same error as you.
This suggests that this is not an issue with the compiler/optimization, but rather incompatibility between gcovr 6.0 and gcov 12.2.0.
Can you try downgrading to gcovr 4.2?

Error in console suggest bug in gcov: https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=68080
hmm, the same gcov has no problems running with b5bc088529 but fails on the following bc8b7dd6dd

> hmm, the same gcov has no problems running with [b5bc088](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/b5bc088529269dd70210d42366f5d20e24658fc3) but fails on [bc8b7dd](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/bc8b7dd6dd36e0ae6b256353bf967c3568b907a7)

As the bug describes, there are threading issues - as I understand it, at the same time something is reading counters and writing them.
This is totally true for this case as we are trying to get coverage for the code of the function that is reading those counters, thus when it is executing, it is writing them at the same time ;)

Still, my change can trigger that bug, as it adds a branch, which may influence which counters are produced or the timing when they are updated.
This means that it may be just a coincidence for specific compiler, optimization level, and code.
As I understand, the same issue may still happen in any other line in this particular file, it is just a matter of how the compiler arranges code or how execution happens.
The issue remains, counters are updated and read at the same time.

My proposal would be to follow suggestion from gcovr doc - ignore this error/bug:
https://gcovr.com/en/6.0/guide/gcov_parser.html#negative-hit-counts

What do you think?

> My proposal would be to follow suggestion from gcovr doc - ignore this error/bug

not sure I understand your point - how to ignore it ?
This issue happens not only for the hello_world sample, and #64397 helps to get coverage working again.

> > My proposal would be to follow suggestion from gcovr doc - ignore this error/bug
> 
> not sure I understand your point - how to ignore it ? This issue happens not only for the hello_world sample, and #64397 helps to get coverage working again.

This error can be ignored by adding an option to gcovr call: --gcov-ignore-parse-errors=negative_hits.warn
This can be added here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/scripts/pylib/twister/twisterlib/coverage.py#L224

I suggest that because even with your change #64397, others, with different compilers or optimization levels can be hit by the same problem but at different locations in this file.

Additionally, this ignore option (and this error message) was introduced at gcovr 6.0.
So to add it, this needs to be updated too:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/scripts/requirements-build-test.txt#L13

Looking here:
https://github.com/gcovr/gcovr/issues/583#issuecomment-1340762818
LCOV is ignoring such case by default.
@nordic-piks, thank you for your workaround suggestion, please see it in #64406

> As the bug describes, there are threading issues - as I understand it, at the same time something is reading counters and writing them.

no threading issues, but is seems gcovr is now missing function call it expects (in .c source) which is replaced by an assembler snippet. - https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64397/files#r1372794902
